3.happening: We create a map from each email to a node id.
3.invariant: Each distinct email maps to one id.

4.happening: We create the list of emails by id.
4.why: The id indexes back to the email text.

5.why: A merged account keeps its owner's name.
5.invariant: owner[id] names the account of that email.

6.happening: We create the graph's adjacency list.
6.why: Edges connect emails in the same account.

8.why: It holds a name and its emails.
8.invariant: account[0] is the name; the rest are emails.

9.why: It labels every email in this account.

10.happening: We start at the account's first email.
10.why: Index 0 is the name, so emails begin at 1.

11.happening: We register email index {ei} of this account.
11.why: Every email must become a node.

11.happening: All of this account's emails are registered.
11.why: The account has no more emails.
11.invariant: Every email of the account is now a node.

12.why: We check whether it is already a node.
12.invariant: email is the account's ei-th entry.

13.happening: We check whether '{email}' is already registered.
13.why: Each distinct email becomes exactly one node.
13.invariant: A repeat email reuses its existing node.

14.happening: We assign '{email}' the next node id.
14.invariant: Ids are assigned in first-seen order.

15.happening: We add '{email}' to the email list.
15.why: So the id maps back to the text.

16.why: The account name travels with the email.

17.happening: We give the new email an empty neighbour list.

18.happening: We move to the next email.
18.why: Every email of the account is registered.

19.happening: We read account {ai} again to add edges.
19.why: Now that all emails are nodes, we connect them.
19.invariant: Every account contributes its internal edges.

21.why: We connect the first email to each other one.
21.invariant: A star of edges connects the account's emails.

22.happening: We start at the account's second email.
22.why: The first is the anchor; others link to it.

23.happening: We connect email {ei} to the first email.
23.why: Emails in one account belong together.
23.invariant: All the account's emails share one component.

23.happening: This account's emails are all linked.
23.invariant: The account forms one connected piece.

24.why: It links to the account's first email.

25.invariant: other is now a neighbour of first.

26.happening: We link node {other} back to node {first}.
26.why: Both directions of an undirected edge.
26.invariant: first is now a neighbour of other.

27.happening: We move to the next email.
27.why: Every email links to the first.

28.happening: We build the drawable graph nodes.
28.why: The stage shows one node per email.

29.happening: We add the node for email id {i}.
29.why: Each email becomes a labelled vertex.
29.invariant: Nodes are created for every email.

30.happening: We add a node labelled by its email.
30.why: The label makes the merge readable.

33.why: Each adjacency becomes a possible edge.

34.why: It may pair with {i} to form an edge.

35.why: Using smaller-first avoids drawing it twice.

35.happening: We skip the edge {i}-{nb} (its twin was drawn).
35.why: The undirected edge is already recorded.

36.happening: We record the edge between {i} and {nb}.

37.why: DFS marks each email visited once.

39.why: No component has been explored yet.

40.why: Each connected component becomes one entry.

41.happening: There is no current DFS node yet.
41.why: cur is set only during a DFS.

42.happening: We start scanning emails for a component root.
42.why: Each component is one merged account.

43.happening: We consider email {start} as a component root.
43.why: Unvisited emails begin a new component.
43.invariant: Emails before start are already merged.

44.happening: Email {start} is unvisited — start a new component.
44.why: Each connected component is explored once.
44.invariant: A component is rooted at its first-found email.

44.happening: Email {start} is already merged — skip it.
44.why: It belongs to an earlier component.

45.why: It collects the emails reachable from the root.
45.invariant: comp holds one merged account's emails.

46.happening: We seed the DFS stack with the root.
46.invariant: The stack holds nodes to explore.

47.happening: We mark the root email visited.
47.why: So it is not collected twice.

48.happening: The DFS stack has {len(stack)} email(s) to explore.
48.why: DFS continues until the component is fully collected.
48.invariant: Every stacked email joins this component.

49.happening: We pop email node {node_id} from the stack.
49.why: DFS explores the most recently found email.

50.why: It is being collected and expanded.
50.invariant: cur is the active email node.

51.happening: We add its email to the component.
51.why: Every reachable email belongs to this account.

53.invariant: nb is adjacent to the current email.

54.happening: Neighbour {nb} is unvisited — add it to the component.
Neighbour {nb} is already in a component.
54.invariant: Each email joins exactly one component.

55.why: So it is collected only once.

57.happening: We clear the current node after the component.
57.why: No email is current while scanning.

58.happening: We sort the component's emails alphabetically.
58.invariant: comp is now in alphabetical order.

59.happening: We start the merged account with the owner name.
59.why: Each account entry begins with the name.

60.why: The account lists all its emails.
60.invariant: Emails follow the name in order.

61.why: It belongs to this merged account.
61.invariant: merged holds name + emails so far.

63.happening: We move to the next email.
63.why: Every email must be rooted or skipped.

64.why: Every email has been assigned to a component.
64.invariant: Accounts sharing an email are merged.

init.happening: Index emails as nodes and link same-account emails.

loop.happening: Root a DFS or expand a component.
loop.why: Each component is one merged account.

check.happening: Test a component root or an unvisited neighbour.

update.happening: Collect an email, mark visited, or build the account.

move.happening: Pop, push, or advance the scan.
move.why: DFS and the outer scan move deterministically.
